roles.title: Assistant Editor
roles.description: Organize footage, sync audio, prep timelines, and support the lead editor.

roles.title: Camera Operator
roles.description: Operate camera, frame shots, and collaborate with DP on visual storytelling.
roles.flavor: The frame is your canvas. Light is your paint.

roles.title: Colorist
roles.description: Grade footage for mood, continuity, and visual style across the entire project.

roles.title: Gaffer
roles.description: Design and execute the lighting plan. Collaborate with DP to shape the visual look.
roles.flavor: Light writes the story. Shadow directs the eye.

roles.title: Production Assistant
roles.description: Support the set: manage call sheets, coordinate talent, handle logistics, and keep the day on schedule.
roles.flavor: The PA makes the production possible.

roles.title: Script Supervisor
roles.description: Track continuity, coverage, and timing on set. Ensure the edit has what it needs.
roles.flavor: Continuity is invisible until it's broken.

roles.title: Sound Designer
roles.description: Create and layer sound effects, ambience, and Foley to build the sonic world.

roles.title: VFX Compositor
roles.description: Integrate CG elements, green screen, and effects into live-action footage seamlessly.
roles.flavor: Invisible effects are the best effects.

cards.name: Attend Color Grade / Mix Session
cards.description: Sit in on a color grading session, sound mix, or online conform review.
cards.flavor: Color and sound are the final rewrite.

cards.name: Complete Partner Film Project
cards.description: Deliver the partner project: creative edit, sound design, color, and final exports per spec.
cards.flavor: Broadcast standards. Festival deadlines.

cards.name: Edit a Production Sequence
cards.description: Cut a scene, segment, or sequence: assemble, rough cut, fine cut, and deliver for review.
cards.flavor: Editing is rewriting with footage.

cards.name: Deliver Film Project
cards.description: Edit the project from assembly to picture lock. Handle notes, conform, and export deliverables.
cards.flavor: Picture lock is a milestone, not the finish.

cards.name: Cut the Trailer
cards.description: Edit the trailer: select beats, pace to music, add graphics, and iterate on feedback.
cards.flavor: Two minutes. Maximum impact.

cards.name: Sync and Organize Dailies
cards.description: Sync audio to picture, organize bins, create stringouts, and prep for the editor.
cards.flavor: Dailies done right save weeks later.

cards.name: Create Motion Graphics Template
cards.description: Build a reusable MOGRT: lower thirds, titles, or transitions with editable controls.
cards.flavor: Templates save hours on every episode.

cards.name: Crew a Short Film
cards.description: Work on a student/indie short: camera, sound, grip, or post. Experience the full pipeline.
cards.flavor: Small crew. Big lessons.

cards.name: Measure Creative Impact
cards.description: Explain how your editing elevated the narrative, pacing, or emotional resonance.
cards.flavor: Invisible edits make the best stories.

cards.name: Trailer Released
cards.description: Partner's trailer launches: track views, engagement, and conversion to ticket sales/streams.
cards.flavor: The trailer sold the show.

cards.name: Partner Film Released
cards.description: Your edit was released: festival selection, broadcast, or client approval. Document the outcome.
cards.flavor: Screened. Selected. Seen.

cards.name: Template Adopted
cards.description: Your MOGRT is used across the production. Document time saved per episode.
cards.flavor: Standardization scales creativity.

cards.name: Sequence in Final Cut
cards.description: Your edited sequence appears in the final deliverable. Document the context and your contribution.
cards.flavor: Your cut made the final cut.

cards.name: Document Film Project Learnings
cards.description: Write a post-mortem: creative challenges, technical workflow, collaboration, and festival strategy.
cards.flavor: Every film teaches a new workflow.

cards.name: Log Edit Hours & Reflection
cards.description: Record hours and reflect on creative choices, director feedback, and technical problem-solving.
cards.flavor: Every cut is a decision. Every revision is growth.

cards.name: Trailer Review Deck
cards.description: Present trailer versions with rationale: structure, music choices, pacing, and test screening data.
cards.flavor: Data defends creative choices.

cards.name: Template Documentation
cards.description: Document the MOGRT: controls, use cases, font requirements, and version history.
cards.flavor: A template without docs is a mystery box.

cards.name: Sequence Reflection
cards.description: Write a reflection on the edit: pacing, storytelling, sound design, and lessons learned.
cards.flavor: The best edit serves the story.

cards.name: Showcase Partner Film Work
cards.description: Present your partner work: brief, rough cut evolution, director collaboration, and final deliverable.
cards.flavor: Show the journey from assembly to answer print.

cards.name: Short Film Feedback
cards.description: Collect feedback from the director/producer on your contribution to the production.
cards.flavor: Set etiquette matters as much as skill.

cards.name: Book Post House Visit
cards.description: Arrange a visit to a post-production facility. Confirm date, NDA, and suite access.
cards.flavor: See where the magic gets polished.

cards.name: Find Film Festival Volunteer
cards.description: Volunteer at a film festival: projection, guest services, or filmmaker hospitality.
cards.flavor: Festivals run on volunteer passion.

cards.name: Trailer Strategy Session
cards.description: Align with partner on trailer goals: audience, tone, key beats, platform specs, and approval chain.
cards.flavor: A trailer is a promise. Keep it.

cards.name: Partner Production Requirements
cards.description: Agree on deliverables with an industry partner: trailer, sizzle reel, or episodic editing.
cards.flavor: Partners need storytellers who hit deadlines.

cards.name: Set Up Project Template
cards.description: Create project template: bin structure, sequence settings, export presets, and keyboard shortcuts.
cards.flavor: Template once. Use forever.

cards.name: Confirm Placement Details
cards.description: Agree tasks, dates, and hours with the production company; confirm your supervisor and call sheets.
cards.flavor: Call time is sacred. Be ready.

cards.name: Complete Production Onboarding
cards.description: Learn the workflow: NLE setup, media management, naming conventions, and backup protocols.
cards.flavor: Organization is the editor's superpower.

cards.name: Understand the Film Brief
cards.description: Clarify the brief: genre, tone, runtime, deliverables (festival DCP, broadcast, social cuts), deadline.
cards.flavor: Deliverables define the workflow.

cards.name: Build a Sponsor Activation
cards.description: Design a small on-site or online activity for a sponsor's brand.
cards.flavor: Sponsors fund the scene — treat them well.

cards.name: Coordinate Volunteer Roles
cards.description: Assign shifts, brief volunteers on their roles, and set up a communication channel for the day.
cards.flavor: Herd management, esports edition.

cards.name: Complete Partner Task
cards.description: Complete the agreed task and ask the partner for feedback.
cards.flavor: Professional feedback is worth more than a grade.

cards.name: Complete Partner Project
cards.description: Work with an industry partner, act on feedback and deliver agreed outcomes.
cards.flavor: Professional feedback is the fastest way to level up.

cards.name: Complete Placement Tasks
cards.description: Choose a focus — event operations, streaming support, social media, player support, or equipment setup — and do the work.
cards.flavor: This is where the CV entry actually gets written.

cards.name: Deliver the Live Brief
cards.description: Finish and present work to the brief. Respond to feedback and iterate.
cards.flavor: Done is better than perfect. Shipped is better than done.

cards.name: Finish Skills Assignment
cards.description: Complete a course assignment that demonstrates subject knowledge relevant to your role.
cards.flavor: Grades open doors. Skills keep them open.

cards.name: Revise After Feedback
cards.description: Improve work using specific feedback. Shows growth mindset and resilience.
cards.flavor: First draft is for you. Second draft is for them.

cards.name: Run a Coaching Session
cards.description: Deliver a one-to-one or small-group coaching moment focused on a specific skill.
cards.flavor: The best coaches listen more than they speak.

cards.name: Measure Your Contribution
cards.description: Explain what changed because of your work, using a result, feedback or clear example.
cards.flavor: Show the difference your contribution made.

cards.name: Share Partner Feedback
cards.description: Record the partner's response to your completed work and how it met their objectives.
cards.flavor: External validation is the gold standard of achievement.

cards.name: Share Partner Outcome
cards.description: Present the finished result to the partner and explain how you used their feedback.
cards.flavor: A strong partnership leaves both sides with something useful.

cards.name: Show Placement Impact
cards.description: Summarise the result of your placement work and how it helped the esports team or event.
cards.flavor: Show what changed because you were there.

cards.name: Showcase Placement Result
cards.description: Present the final outcome of your placement work — a demo, report, or deliverable — and explain its impact.
cards.flavor: The best placements end with a story worth telling.

cards.name: Ask for a Reference
cards.description: Request written feedback from someone who supervised your work.
cards.flavor: A reference is a vote of confidence in writing.

cards.name: Write a CV Achievement
cards.description: Describe your contribution, the skill you used and the measurable outcome.
cards.flavor: Don't list duties. List impact.

cards.name: Daily Log & Reflection
cards.description: Record what you did, what you learned and how it connects to your target role.
cards.flavor: Experience unrecorded is experience forgotten.

cards.name: Debug & Learning Log
cards.description: Document a bug or unexpected issue you hit, the steps you took to diagnose it, and what you learned.
cards.flavor: Every bug is a lesson in disguise.

cards.name: Distinction Earned
cards.description: Bonus evidence: subject excellence.
cards.flavor: Excellence isn't an accident. It's the result of intention.

cards.name: Document Brief Learnings
cards.description: Write up what the brief taught you about your role, the client's needs, and your design decisions.
cards.flavor: A written record is the bridge between doing and reflecting.

cards.name: Reflect on Coaching Feedback
cards.description: Document how coaching conversations helped a player improve their performance or mindset.
cards.flavor: Coaching lives in the follow-through.

cards.name: Log Placement Hours & Reflection
cards.description: Record your hours and write what you did, what you learned, and how it connects to your target job.
cards.flavor: Evidence is what turns a placement into a reference.

cards.name: Placement Reflection
cards.description: Write a mid-point or final reflection on your placement tasks, challenges overcome, and skills developed.
cards.flavor: Reflection turns experience into evidence.

cards.name: Present & Reflect on Feedback
cards.description: Present your work, note the feedback, and save the final version for your portfolio.
cards.flavor: Feedback is free improvement if you actually listen.

cards.name: Record Industry Insight
cards.description: Write up one thing you learned and how it changes your view of the job.
cards.flavor: Insight only counts once it's written down.

cards.name: Reliability Check-In
cards.description: Explain how you'll confirm your shift and contact the organiser if plans change.
cards.flavor: Reliability is a skill, not a personality trait.

cards.name: Revise With Feedback
cards.description: Use the partner's feedback to improve your work before it goes in your portfolio.
cards.flavor: The revision is where the real learning happens.

cards.name: Save Portfolio Evidence
cards.description: Keep a finished work sample and explain your role, tools used and outcome.
cards.flavor: Your portfolio is your proof. Make it undeniable.

cards.name: Showcase Partner Work
cards.description: Document the deliverables produced during the partnership, highlighting your specific contribution and the skills applied.
cards.flavor: The best partnerships leave a paper trail of success.

cards.name: Volunteer Feedback
cards.description: Collect and record feedback from the event organiser or fellow volunteers about your contribution.
cards.flavor: A thank-you note is worth more than a certificate.

cards.name: Agree Dates & Times
cards.description: Confirm the schedule and hours in writing. Must fit college hours (8:30am–5:30pm, max 8hr day).
cards.flavor: Verbal agreements evaporate. Written ones stick.

cards.name: Agree Your Role
cards.description: Clarify tasks, responsibilities, supervision and what you'll produce.
cards.flavor: Undefined work is unpaid work. Define it.

cards.name: Confirm Partner Project
cards.description: Find out who the industry partner is, what the project involves, when sessions happen, and what they expect you to produce.
cards.flavor: Partnerships work best with clear expectations on both sides.

cards.name: Confirm Venue Logistics
cards.description: Book the venue, confirm access, arrange equipment, and create a run sheet for the event.
cards.flavor: The devil is in the details, and the angels love a well-run event.

cards.name: Employer Contact
cards.description: Get a named contact and a way to reach them — email, phone, LinkedIn.
cards.flavor: A name on a spreadsheet becomes a mentor in real life.

cards.name: Find an Organisation
cards.description: Identify a studio, team, publisher or community that matches your career goal.
cards.flavor: Every journey starts with a destination in mind.

cards.name: Partner Expectations
cards.description: Find out what the industry partner expects you to produce and how they'll support you.
cards.flavor: Partners don't want free labour. They want fresh perspective.

cards.name: Review the Brief
cards.description: Read the brief, identify the audience, check the deadline, and decide what you'll make.
cards.flavor: A clear brief saves three drafts later.

cards.name: Stage the Run Sheet
cards.description: Create a detailed run sheet with roles, timings, contacts and contingency plans for the event.
cards.flavor: A good run sheet saves the day before anyone knows there was a problem.

cards.name: Travel & Access Plan
cards.description: Check location, travel, equipment needs and any access requirements.
cards.flavor: The best plan fails if you can't get through the door.

cards.name: Understand the Brief
cards.description: Clarify the audience, deliverable, deadline and success criteria with the client.
cards.flavor: A brief misunderstood is a project doomed.

cards.name: Wild Card: Evidence Boost
cards.description: A second pair of eyes strengthens your evidence. Use this card in place of a Proof card for a Block Placement.
cards.flavor: Evidence worth keeping is evidence worth boosting.

cards.name: Wild Card: Extra Time
cards.description: A brief extension to get the work right. Use this card in place of an Action card for a Live Project Brief.
cards.flavor: Time is the one resource you can never get back.

cards.name: Wild Card: Tutor Advice
cards.description: A quick check-in with your tutor. Use this card in place of a Setup card for Volunteering.
cards.flavor: Sometimes the right words at the right time change everything.

cards.name: Wild Card: Careers Team
cards.description: The Careers & Employability team steps in. Use this card in place of any Setup, Action or Proof card for a Block Placement.
cards.flavor: They've seen every version of this problem before.

cards.name: Wild Card: Mentor Advice
cards.description: A mentor points you in the right direction. Use this card in place of any Setup, Action or Proof card for a Live Project Brief.
cards.flavor: Sometimes the fastest route is someone who's done it before.

sets.name: Block Placement
sets.why: A placement gives practical experience and, if it goes well, an employer reference.

sets.name: Employer Visit
sets.why: A visit builds industry understanding and useful contacts.

sets.name: Volunteering
sets.why: Volunteering shows reliability, initiative and teamwork.

sets.name: Live Project Brief
sets.why: A finished brief creates a portfolio piece that shows you can respond to a client's needs.

sets.name: Industry Partnership
sets.why: A partnership gives you specialist feedback and experience working with professionals.
